Aggregate catch and effort by assessment region

catcheffort_byregion.Rd

Assigns gridded catch and effort data to assessment regions and sums them by region, species and gear. Regions with no data for a given species and gear combination are retained with zeros, so the output is a complete grid.

Usage

catcheffort_byregion(
  catcheffort,
  assessment_region,
  crs = 4326,
  show_plot = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

catcheffort

A data frame of gridded catch and effort, such as the output of get_aggregated_catcheffort(). Must contain the columns lond, latd, SP_CODE, GEAR_CODE, sum_catch_mt, hhooks, VESS_N, days and sets.

assessment_region

An sf object of assessment region polygons with a region_id column, such as the output of as_region() or get_md2_shp().

crs

Coordinate reference system of catcheffort coordinates, passed to sf::st_as_sf(). Defaults to 4326 (WGS 84).

show_plot

Logical. If TRUE, prints a map of the aggregated catch overlaid with the assessment regions before aggregating. Defaults to FALSE.

...

Additional arguments passed to plot_aggregated_catch() when show_plot = TRUE, for example facet_by = GEAR_CODE. Ignored otherwise.

Value

A tibble with one row per combination of region_id, SP_CODE and GEAR_CODE, containing the summed sum_catch_mt, hhooks, VESS_N, days and sets. Combinations with no data are filled with 0.

Details

Grid cells are assigned to regions using their centre point. The cell size is taken as the smallest gap between unique latd values, and each coordinate is shifted by half that gap (lond/latd are assumed to be the south-west corner of each cell, and the same resolution is assumed for longitude). Because centres sit away from the cell edges, cells are not lost when a region boundary lies on a grid line (for example, at 150°). Region boundaries that cut through the middle of a cell will assign it to whichever region contains its centre.

Cells are matched with sf::st_within(), so any cell centre falling exactly on a region boundary, or outside every region, is dropped.

VESS_N is summed across cells, so vessels operating in more than one cell are counted more than once. Treat it as vessel-cell counts rather than unique vessels.

See also

get_aggregated_catcheffort(), as_region(), get_md2_shp()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Define a simple two-region assessment area from vertices
bb <- tibble::tribble(
  ~region_id , ~lon , ~lat ,
  "1"        ,  110 ,   -0 ,
  "1"        ,  110 ,   20 ,
  "1"        ,  150 ,   20 ,
  "1"        ,  150 ,    0 ,
  "2"        ,  160 ,   -0 ,
  "2"        ,  160 ,   -5 ,
  "2"        ,  190 ,   -5 ,
  "2"        ,  190 ,  -10 ,
  "2"        ,  200 ,  -10 ,
  "2"        ,  200 ,    0
)

x <- get_aggregated_catcheffort(
  flag = "KI",
  year = 2020:2025,
  species = "YFT",
  gear = c("L", "S")
)
y <- as_region(bb)
# or get regions from MD2 by model_id or species:
# y <- get_md2_shp(model_id = 130)

# Aggregate and plot, faceting the map by gear
catcheffort_byregion(x, y, show_plot = TRUE, facet_by = GEAR_CODE)
} # }
